title: Resolving the binary components of the outbursting protostar HBC 494 with ALMA
question: Resolve the substructure/asymmetry in the disk of the outbursting protostar HBC 494 to determine its nature and examine the surrounding gas kinematics at small and large scales.

data.angular_resolution: 0.142 arcsec (first night); 0.027 arcsec (second night); 41.2 x 29.8 mas (combined continuum)
data.sensitivity: ~0.034 mJy/beam (continuum); 1.9, 3.6, and 2.6 mJy/beam for 12CO, 13CO, and C18O respectively

evidence.quote: HBC 494 is a Class I protostar, located in the Orion molecular cloud at a distance of 414±7 pc (Menten et al. 2007)

what.value: Sample of 14 resolved FUors and EXors and Class 0/I systems for dust mass vs radius comparison

evidence.quote: The dust mass vs radius comparison between HBC 494 N and HBC 494 S, a sample of 14 resolved FUors and EXors (extracted from Hales et al. 2020) and Class 0/I systems (Tobin et al. 2020), can be seen in figure 8.

To generate this plot, we obtained data from Kóspál et al. (2017); Hales et al. (2018); Cieza et al. (2018); Takami et al. (2019); Cruz-Sáenz de Miera et al. (2019); Pérez et al. (2020); Hales et al. (2020).

external_data.citation: Kóspál et al. (2017); Hales et al. (2018); Cieza et al. (2018); Takami et al. (2019); Cruz-Sáenz de Miera et al. (2019); Pérez et al. (2020); Hales et al. (2020); Tobin et al. (2020)

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate, concatenate, and image 1.3 mm continuum visibilities
recipe.method: Fix visibilities phase center, perform 1 iteration of self-calibration on each night's dataset, concatenate short and long baseline measurement sets using concat, and synthesize final continuum image with tclean.
key_parameters: Phase center: J2000 05h40m27.448s -07d27m29.65s; Briggs robust = 0.5; pixel scale = 1.5 mas

recipe.goal: Characterize continuum disk properties (fluxes, sizes, position angles, inclinations) and radial profiles
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussians to the resolved binary components in the continuum image using CASA imfit, derive disk inclinations from the deconvolved aspect ratios, and extract radial brightness profiles in elliptical apertures.
key_parameters: RMS measured in a circular region with a radius of 225 mas without emission
assumptions: Disks are circular when face-on and elliptical when inclined

recipe.goal: Estimate dust and gas masses of the two circumstellar disks
recipe.method: Compute dust mass from integrated 1.3 mm continuum flux density using the optically thin isothermal dust emission formula, and multiply by gas-to-dust ratio for gas mass.
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission, distance d = 414 pc, isothermal dust temperature T_dust = 20 K, gas-to-dust mass ratio M_gas/M_dust = 100, dust opacity kappa_nu = 10 (nu / 10^12 Hz) cm^2 g^-1

recipe.goal: Continuum subtraction, spectral line imaging, and moment/channel map analysis at large (8000 au) and small (150 au) scales
recipe.method: Fix phase center, subtract continuum in uv-plane with uvcontsub, image 12CO, 13CO, and C18O cubes with tclean, and generate channel maps, moment 0 and moment 1 maps, spectral profiles, and spatial cuts before and after continuum subtraction.
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 0.5; Hogbom deconvolver; pixel scale = 6 mas; spectral widths: 1 km/s (12CO) and 0.3 km/s (13CO, C18O); velocity ranges: -6 to 18 km/s (total / 12CO, excluding 1 to 5 km/s for cloud contamination), 0 to 11 km/s (13CO, C18O)

score_reason: Raw data are public, CASA version and core imaging/fitting tasks (tclean, concat, uvcontsub, imfit) and key parameters (robust=0.5, pixel scales, velocity ranges, dust mass formula and constants) are explicitly stated; slight deductions for missing self-calibration solint and uvcontsub channel selection details.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data (2016.1.00630.S) with a straightforward imaging + CASA imfit + analytical dust mass recipe yielding clear, high-SNR numeric results for the binary separation, disk fluxes, deconvolved sizes, inclinations, and masses.
